# Chicago Lease Renewal Review

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

Given the notice date, current lease end date, and 2-year tenancy, the main goals are to confirm the basis for the increase, check what the lease allows, and negotiate from a clear position.

## Lease Renewal Checklist and Negotiation Points

| Area | What to Ask or Review | Why It Matters |
|---|---|---|
| Increase details | What is the current rent, the new rent, and when does the increase start? | Confirms the math and timing. |
| Notice terms | Does the lease require a specific notice period or format for renewal changes? | Helps you compare the notice against the contract. |
| Renewal options | Is this a renewal, month-to-month conversion, or a new fixed-term lease? | Changes your leverage and flexibility. |
| Comparable rents | What nearby units or recent renewals support the 12% increase? | Lets you ask for justification or a smaller bump. |
| Unit condition | Will any repairs, upgrades, or services be included with the higher rent? | Useful if the increase is tied to improvements. |
| Fees and concessions | Are parking, storage, pets, utilities, or admin fees changing too? | Prevents surprise cost increases beyond base rent. |
| Lease changes | Are there any new clauses in the renewal lease? | Renewal packages often add terms beyond rent. |
| Timing | Can you get more time to review or sign? | Creates room to negotiate before the deadline. |
| Alternatives | What is the month-to-month rate or a shorter renewal term? | Gives fallback options if the increase feels too high. |

### Practical Questions to Ask the Landlord
- What is driving the 12% increase?
- Is this increase based on market rent, property taxes, operating costs, or improvements?
- Can you offer a smaller increase for a longer renewal term?
- Is the increase negotiable if I renew quickly?
- Are there any concessions available, such as a lower first-month rate or waived fees?
- Will the renewal keep the same lease terms except for rent?
- Are any maintenance issues being addressed before renewal?
- If I do not renew, what is the move-out process and deadline?

### Points to Review in the Lease
- Renewal notice deadline and required delivery method
- Rent increase clause and any limits on renewal pricing
- Month-to-month conversion terms after the lease ends
- Late fee, grace period, and payment method rules
- Maintenance and repair responsibilities
- Entry notice rules for inspections or showings
- Fee changes for pets, parking, storage, or amenities
- Any automatic renewal language
- Termination, holdover, and move-out notice requirements
- Signature deadlines and whether the renewal supersedes prior terms

## Polite but Firm Negotiation Email Draft

Subject: Lease Renewal Discussion

Hi [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

Thank you for sending the renewal notice. I have enjoyed living at the property for the past two years and would like to continue my tenancy.

I reviewed the proposed 12% rent increase and wanted to ask whether there is any flexibility on the renewal terms. The increase is higher than I was expecting, so I would appreciate any room to discuss a more moderate adjustment, especially if I renew for another fixed term.

If helpful, I would also be open to discussing other options such as:
- a smaller rent increase in exchange for a longer renewal term
- a shorter renewal term
- keeping the current terms otherwise unchanged
- any available concessions or fee adjustments

Please let me know whether there is any flexibility and, if so, what options you can offer. I’d like to resolve this promptly and in a way that works for both sides.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Best,
[Your Name]
[Unit Number]
[Phone Number]
